C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-2.Summary: One deliverable: the reconciliation `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY` could not deliver under its own ratified criteria. The predecessor's work is committed and stands — sixteen staged findings flushed, the chartered `C-INDEX-METRIC-2` row minted for the already-archived bundle, one `--retire` paying `F205` and moving the row — and the record end state it produced holds (the shipped production assertions over the real record are green at this commit, and the shipped validator returns zero findings). But `validate:ci` is red at this commit: the occupancy table in the `computeElementSpans` test "pairs every element of the real record files at their committed bytes" (`src/artifact/xml.test.ts:600`-628, measured at this commit) hard-codes how many elements each of the seven record files contains, and the flush moved four of the seven pins. The predecessor's `AC-NO-SRC` forbids touching any `src/` path except the retirement suite, so the bundle cannot be made green without violating a ratified criterion; under `D27` an approved artifact is repaired only by supersede, and this bundle is the replacement. The shape follows the `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3` precedent (`3ba0d77`): criteria that assert an already-performed end state and are invariant under this bundle's own close, not a re-run of the performed work. The repair is governed by `D30` for what it rules — a spec may not pin scalar counts of a file it changes into its hard Constraints, and what is forbidden is a Constraint whose truth expires the next time anyone writes the file — and this bundle extends that reasoning to test assertions over the record, a form `D30` does not state and does not reach: the transcribed counts do not go back in and are replaced by relations the record files themselves determine, which catch the corruption the counts were guarding and never fire on legitimate growth. Binding live rulings `D27` (supersede is the route), `D30` (the defect class being repaired, extended to the test surface by this bundle), `D28` and `D28.1` (the enforcement this bundle asserts green, and never changes), `D11`, `F136.1` (one module enumeration). Name searched 2026-09-09 at this commit: no archive directory and no `Row` in either registry layer carries `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-2`; the name is new.
C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-2.Problem:
`validate:ci` is red on exactly one test at this commit. `bun test src/artifact/xml.test.ts` exits 1 (read without a pipe): the test "pairs every element of the real record files at their committed bytes" fails its occupancy pin for `findings.xml` — expected 195, received 210 — at `src/artifact/xml.test.ts:617`. The full `bun run test` reports 1787 pass, 3 skip, 1 fail across 63 files, the single failure being this test; every later `validate:ci` stage that the `&&` chain never reached was run separately at this commit and exits 0, including both record validators over the moved record — so the whole red is this one assertion and the whole repair is this one file.
The table the test carries (`src/artifact/xml.test.ts:603`-609) is a human transcription of the record's element occupancy. It arrived with `C-RECORD-PARSE` (PR #82, pins 213 / 58 / 61 / 5 / 12 / 36 / 337) and was reconciled once, by hand, in `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-3` (PR #83, pins 195 / 77 / 61 / 5 / 12 / 44 / 338). The flush moved four of the seven again — the engine's true counts, measured by the shipped parser over direct children filtered on the genre tag, are 210 / 78 / 61 / 5 / 12 / 45 / 354 — and the deltas reconstruct the predecessor's committed work exactly: sixteen `Finding` elements and sixteen index `Entry` lines landed, one `Finding` (`F205`) and the freshly minted row moved to their retired siblings in the same wave. A transcription whose truth expires the next time anyone writes the file is the defect class `D30` names for spec Constraints — its own words: what is forbidden is a Constraint whose truth expires the next time anyone writes the file — living in a test, which `D30` does not reach: its rule binds a spec's hard Constraints, not suite assertions. This bundle establishes the broader form and says so: a transcribed count in a test expires on the next legitimate record write exactly as a transcribed count in a Constraint does, and this bundle exists because one did. Each reconciliation has been a human editing numbers the file itself could have determined.
The predecessor cannot deliver the repair. Its ratified `AC-NO-SRC` forbids any `src/` change except `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`, and the repair file is `src/artifact/xml.test.ts`; making the suite green would have violated a ratified criterion, so under `D27` the route is supersede. The authority performs the supersede once this spec exists; this bundle writes no record file, edits no `scripts/` file, and performs no supersede itself. What it delivers is the two things the predecessor could not: the assertion that the end state its predecessor produced stands, and the replacement of the occupancy pins with relations that hold under every legitimate write.

Goals.Goal: The end state, asserted — never re-performed. The flush already happened; this bundle writes no record file and asserts the committed result. The asserted end state: in `findings.xml`, no `Finding` whose token is `F205`, while `findings-retired.xml` holds exactly one `Finding` with `id="f205"`, `status="retired"`, carrying the move's `<PaidBy>C-INDEX-METRIC-2</PaidBy>` stamp; `f206` through `f220` live, each exactly once across both findings files with the agreeing index `Entry` layer; the `C-INDEX-METRIC-2` row present in `registry-retired.xml` as a retired chartered row and absent from live `registry.xml`, its derived payment set exactly `F205`; the `f205` index `Entry` flipped to `layer="retired"` in place; every live root satisfying the shipped roots relations (`base + headroom = ceiling`, `base` equal to its shipped metric read back); and the shipped `validateRecordRetirement` returning zero findings on the production record. Every clause is observed by production assertions the predecessor's plan already shipped into `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` — the flush invariant, the payment invariant, the `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4` roots invariant and the production invariant that runs the shipped validator over the production record and reports planted eligibility on a mutated copy — all of them green at this commit (suite 67 pass, 0 fail), and this bundle edits none of them. The criterion is invariant under this bundle's own close and under the predecessor's supersede: neither writes the record, and neither the close ceremony's move nor a fresh `--retire` over a throwaway copy of the end state reports anything but moved 0 (driven at this commit). Failure: a named element still live, missing, or carrying a disagreeing layer; a root relation broken; the validator returning findings.

The repair — the occupancy pins replaced by file-determined relations, never updated. In `src/artifact/xml.test.ts`, the pairing test keeps its substance (all seven real record files parsed at their committed bytes, root non-null, `computeElementSpans` succeeding and every direct genre child paired, index `Entry` elements self-closing) and loses its transcription: the `expected` column and every other transcribed element count of a record file are gone. In their place the test asserts relations the files themselves determine, measured green at this commit and invariant under every legitimate write: (a) identity — every direct genre child carries its genre identity attribute (`Finding` id, `Decision` id, `Row` name, `Entry` id) and the identities are unique within their file; (b) conservation — for each of the findings, rulings and registry genres, the live and retired identity sets are disjoint, so every element lives in exactly one layer; (c) index bookkeeping — the `decisions.xml` root's persisted `base` equals the count of its direct `Entry` children with `layer="live"` (the `C-INDEX-METRIC-2` live-entry metric, read back through this repository's parser). The relations catch what the counts were guarding — wholesale record corruption that stays well-formed and pairs cleanly, which every other assertion in the same test lets through: duplication breaks (a); copy-instead-of-move breaks (b), a class no shipped check currently catches for non-eligible elements; a dropped or wrongly flipped `Entry` breaks (c); and every legitimate write keeps all three true, because a flush appends fresh identities, a move removes from the live layer what it adds to the retired one, a flip changes only a layer attribute, and the persist rewrites `base` with its read-back. The discriminating probe is the growth mutation: on a throwaway copy of the repository, append one fresh `Finding` and its `Entry` to the copy's record and re-persist the copy's roots exactly as the next flush's wave would — base re-derived from the file by the shipped persist formulas, the write that keeps the index relation true — and the relations stay green, and any restored count dies. That is the property the pins lacked, and the reason the relation, not the number, is the replacement. A second shipped assertion, the house body-shaped single-definition form, guards the rule itself: the test file's pairing test carries no transcribed record element count in any form, so the occupancy table cannot quietly return. If any relation proves non-assertable at implementation time, the bundle stops and reports rather than reintroducing a count.

The supersede window, and what this bundle does not perform. The authority supersedes `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY` once this spec exists — an outward-facing act under `D27` that this spec requests but does not perform. The move edits only the predecessor bundle's paths under `.ngrace/changes/`, writes no record file, and mints no eligibility: no `Row` in either registry layer carries the name `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY`, so the move the close ceremony runs for this bundle is a no-op (`F196`'s post-close rule, inherited from the predecessor), and a `--retire` over a throwaway copy of the end state reports moved 0 (driven at this commit). Every byte-invariance criterion below therefore holds in the only state where `CloseEvidence` is ever evaluated, and each exclusion that keeps it satisfiable is named with its reason in the criterion.

Constraints.Constraint: Ceremony tier T1: one `src/` test file, this bundle's own artifacts; no record write, no `scripts/` edit, no runtime file of any graph module edited. The occupancy prohibition, binding on the plan. The repaired test must not carry a transcribed element count of any record file in any form — the `expected` column, a constant, or an inline literal compared against a parsed element count — and every number the test uses about a record file is read back from that file at test time. The replacement relations are exactly the three in the repair Goal; the anti-occupancy guard assertion ships in the same file, in the house body-shaped single-definition form, so the prohibition is machine-observed at close and not a prose promise. The criterion below names the mutation that reddens the guard.

Evidence hygiene, settled lessons. Every criterion below is close-bound: no task carries `Satisfies`, the admissible mapping set is empty, and every criterion is complete `CloseEvidence` except the by-hand one (the `C-RECORD-PARSE` shape). Every `CloseEvidence` `Command` matches a shipped discriminating shape — re-read at `src/artifact/grammar.ts:100`-177 at this commit — and every byte-invariance command names a baseline commit, because the base-less `git diff` form cannot fail (`F210`'s rule). The window of every byte-invariance criterion is this bundle's own diff, stated in the criterion (`F215`'s rule); the commands see tracked edits and deletions only (`F174`) and exclude this bundle's own later archive arrival (`F188`) and the predecessor's sanctioned supersede arrival, named with the `D27` reason in `AC-NO-ARCHIVE-SPEC-EDIT`. `CloseEvidence` is evaluated only in the applied-archive state (`F196`): every criterion below holds there, because neither this bundle's close nor the predecessor's supersede writes the record or any `src/` path. Assertions are cited by their shipped test names; suite line numbers appear only in Assumptions as dated context that expires on any suite edit (`F123`'s law), and no assertion is cited before its shipped name is searched (`F213`'s law). Payer-map claims are observed by the shipped suite assertions, which call the shipped `derivePayerMap` over fixtures that mirror real archive membership (`F212`'s rule) — this bundle re-derives none of that logic. Any test measuring the real repository keeps an explicit generous timeout (`F185`'s rule); the repaired test keeps its 60_000. Every task `Verification` command the later plan records must exit 0 at the stage it is meant to run (`F184`'s refined rule, which rejects judging execution-stage commands at plan time), and task `Verification` and `TargetAssertions` carry no current-mode lint of this project root (`F171`'s rule, checked by hand because the shipped detector misses the `grace.ts` form). Every mutation probe runs on a throwaway copy, never the committed tree: a standalone copy of the record for the CLI instruments, which take a record path argument, and a copy of the repository with its record mutated for the shipped suites, which resolve the production record from their own tree and take no path.
